source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: The AI ecosystem is not zero-sum — frontier labs, open source, neoclouds, inference clouds, and applications can all win simultaneously
summary_extended: Baker argues that the AI ecosystem is fundamentally non-zero-sum, explicitly rejecting the common investor framing that one frontier lab, one cloud provider, or one deployment model must 'win' at the expense of others. His core thesis is that frontier labs (Anthropic, OpenAI), open-source models (Meta's Llama), hyperscaler AI infrastructure (Google TPUs, AWS, Azure), neoclouds, inference clouds, and well-executing application companies can all succeed simultaneously because AI demand is outrunning compute supply — meaning there is room for multiple winners across the stack. The investment implication is that investors should not make binary bets or assume market share is fixed; instead, a broad basket of AI infrastructure and application companies can compound together as the overall market expands. Baker frames this as his core LP-facing thesis and repeats the 'and not or' framing multiple times, suggesting high conviction in the structural view rather than a specific stock call.
